questions.q: What waste does prompt caching eliminate?
options: The need to ever load model weights more than once
Recomputing the KV cache for a shared prefix (e.g. a system prompt) from scratch on every request
The need to ever use a GPU for inference
Duplicate tokenizer vocabularies across requests
questions.explain: Without prompt caching, a shared prefix like a system prompt or few-shot examples gets fully recomputed by prefill on every request, even though its content hasn't changed. Caching it once avoids that repeated cost.

questions.q: How does server-side automatic prefix caching work?
options: It requires the API caller to manually mark every cacheable section
The serving framework hashes incoming prompt prefixes and reuses existing matching PagedAttention blocks automatically
It stores entire conversation histories permanently on disk
It only works if every request is byte-for-byte identical, including the response
questions.explain: Server-side automatic prefix caching (enabled by default in vLLM) hashes incoming prefixes and checks existing cache blocks for a match, reusing them with no API-level configuration needed.

questions.q: What is required for a prompt's prefix to produce a cache hit?
options: The prefix only needs to be approximately similar in meaning
The prefix must match exactly, token for token, since every token's key/value depends on all tokens before it
The prefix must be shorter than 100 tokens
The prefix must come from the same user account every time
questions.explain: Because attention makes every token's key/value depend on all preceding tokens, even a single changed earlier token (like an inserted timestamp) invalidates the cache for everything after that point.

questions.q: Why do production prompts designed for caching put stable content first and variable content last?
options: Because models can only process prompts in reverse order
Because it maximizes how much of the prefix stays identical across requests, maximizing the portion of the prompt that can be served from cache
Because variable content must always come before stable content for the tokenizer to work
Because this ordering has no effect on caching whatsoever
questions.explain: Putting stable, shared content (system instructions, fixed examples) first and variable, per-request content last keeps the largest possible portion of the prompt identical across requests, which is what gets reused from cache.

questions.q: What security consideration does prompt caching raise in multi-tenant serving systems?
options: Prompt caching has no security implications in any deployment
Cache reuse must be scoped so that one tenant's cached prefix content can never leak into another tenant's response
Multi-tenant systems cannot use prompt caching under any circumstances
Only single-tenant systems are vulnerable to any caching issue
questions.explain: If cache blocks were shared across different tenants' requests whenever prefixes matched, that risks leaking one tenant's content into another's response, so production systems scope cache sharing to prevent cross-tenant matches.
